beats.text: How does an API survive 10,000 requests a second?
beats.say: How does an API survive ten thousand requests a second?

beats.text: Without limits, one user can hog the whole server.
beats.say: Without limits, a single user, or one buggy script, can hog the whole server and crash it for everyone.

beats.text: A rate limiter is a bouncer for your API.
beats.say: The fix is a rate limiter. Think of it as a bouncer standing in front of your API.

beats.text: Token bucket: the bucket refills 5 tokens every second.
beats.say: The most popular version is the token bucket. Each user gets a bucket of tokens, and it refills at a steady rate, say five tokens every second.

beats.text: Token available? Request passes. Bucket empty? Error 429.
beats.say: Every request needs a token. Token available? The request passes through. Bucket empty? It's rejected with a four twenty nine, too many requests.
